did_you_know.text: Did you know? Job chapter 4 begins with Eliphaz the Temanite’s reply, making him the first of Job’s friends to speak to him after Job’s speech.
Did you know? Eliphaz reminds Job that in the past he instructed many people, strengthened weak hands, and encouraged those who had stumbled.
Did you know? Eliphaz points out the contrast between Job’s former conduct as someone who strengthened others and his present reaction now that trouble has struck him personally.
Did you know? Eliphaz presents Job’s fear of God, hope, and integrity as foundations that should support him in times of trouble.
Did you know? Eliphaz asks who among the innocent has ever perished, expressing his belief that the blameless and upright do not perish without cause.
Did you know? According to Eliphaz, those who devise iniquity and sow trouble will eventually reap the consequences of their actions.
Did you know? Eliphaz uses the imagery of the lion, the fierce lion, and the young lion to describe how even the powerful can lose their strength and be scattered.
Did you know? Eliphaz describes a message that came to him secretly, of which his ear caught only a whisper.
Did you know? In the night vision, Eliphaz cannot clearly identify the figure before him; he describes a vague form, silence, and a voice that he hears.
Did you know? At the heart of the message in the vision is the question of whether a person can be more righteous or pure than God, emphasizing God’s superiority over humanity.
